As someone starting out as a vegetarian, I noticed a distinct lack of energy. I started cooking with a cast iron pan,and realized that I was probably iron deficient.

Any others have advice on how to manage nutrition, especially for vitamins & minerals for those starting out or considering it? Anything in particular to be aware of?

Iron and B12 were the ones that I was told to watch out for. you can get B12 from eggs, and I keep a bottle of iron supplements that I take once in a while when I feel I need it. I also get the GNC brand "Ultra Mega Green Mens sport" vitamin packs and take them every day, but I'm known for not eating much (or well) and I do work out at the gym often.

I would say get some good multivitamins and and iron supplement for when you need it.

I have a iron / B vitamin table that I take two or three times a week.

It's easy to overdo the carbs and under eat protein as a new vegetarian so just keep an eye what you shove in your gob and you'll be golden.

When I became a vegetarian I also started juicing on a daily basis. Green juice every morning and zero nutritional issues. Also, if you're doing shakes post-workout, throw in a bananna and molasses for iron and b6 and potassium.

eat a wide variety of foods. it can be easy to fall into a trap of preparing the same foods over and over again but eating a varied diet can help both stave off boredom and also make sure you get the nutrients you need.
